info.name: SmartLogistics
info.description:
Auto-generated from every service's OpenAPI schema by `scripts/generate_api_docs.py` (`./dev.sh docs`). Do not edit by hand.

All requests go through the gateway (`base_url`, port 8000).

request.description: Every service fetches this once and verifies tokens locally.

item.name: Authenticate and receive a token pair

request.description:
The access token carries role, warehouse scope and courier id, so every
other service can authorise without calling Identity.

item.name: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair

request.description: Refresh tokens rotate. Replaying a rotated token revokes every session.

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

item.name: Warehouses an operator is scoped to
Scope an operator to a warehouse

request.description:
The warehouse id is checked with the Warehouse service — there is no
foreign key across databases. The operator's sessions are revoked so their
next token carries the new scope.

Address, coordinates, entrance, geofence, phone and hours of active
facilities — nothing about capacity, contacts or layout.
Operators see only the warehouses in their token's scope.

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

request.description:
Only `active` facilities may originate shipments. Shipment and Inventory
learn about the change from the `warehouse.status_changed` event.
Operators see only their warehouses. `available_qty` is a generated column.
Every change leaves a ledger entry. A result below the held quantity is refused.

Operators can only sweep their own warehouses — a `warehouse_id` outside
their scope is refused (the monolith let it through).

item.name: Hold stock for a shipment (all lines or none)

request.description:
Rows are locked in id order, so concurrent requests for the same units
serialise: the first wins and the second gets `insufficient_stock`. The
hold stays *unconfirmed* until `shipment.created` arrives, and returns the
SKU facts Shipment snapshots onto its items.

item.name: Confirm a hold (normally driven by shipment.created)
Create a shipment and hold its stock

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

request.description:
Reserves stock with Inventory first (one synchronous call), then records
the shipment and `shipment.created` in one transaction. With an
`Idempotency-Key`, a retry returns the original response and reuses the
same hold.

Row-scoped: operators see their warehouses, couriers their assignments.
Served entirely from this service's database — no calls to other services.

item.name: Move a shipment to the next state

request.description:
Validated against the state machine; every transition writes an audit
row and a `shipment.status_changed` event. Concurrent changes to the same
shipment cannot both apply: the loser gets 409 `concurrent_update`.
Inventory releases the hold when it receives the status event.
